hook_text: Two ways to place the comma — and they must agree
clip_script:
Everything in this lesson comes down to one question: where does the comma go? And there are two ways to answer it, and they must agree. Way one is counting: add up the decimal places in the two numbers you multiplied, and the answer has that many. Way two is estimating: round each number to something friendly, multiply roughly, and the answer must be near that. If counting says two comma eight two and estimating says about three, you are done. If counting says twenty-eight comma two and estimating says about three, you have miscounted, and you fix it before anyone sees it.

Let me show you how the two ways rescue each other. Zero comma six times zero comma four. Counting: one plus one is two places, and six times four is twenty-four, so zero comma two four. Estimating: a bit more than half of a bit less than a half — about a quarter. Zero comma two four is about a quarter. Agreed.
visual_style: Butcher's scale and petrol pump readouts; a comma sliding along a row of digits until the estimate lights up green
pacing: steady, pausing when the comma lands
call_to_action: Open the full session to place the comma right every time.
